subject: SOC 2 Type II, bridge letter & EU hosting / data transfer Qs
messages:
From: Caroline Larsen <caroline.larsen@eurofintrust.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@eurofintrust.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: SOC 2 Type II & hosting boundary questions

Hi Ben,

We're preparing for our vendor intake and have a few immediate questions about Redwood's SOC 2 Type II coverage and EU hosting controls so we can close our security review. Can you confirm the following?

- Do you have a SOC 2 Type II report that covers the 12-month period ending 2026-06-30? If not, what's the most recent period covered and when is the next report due?
- For our use case (processing EU customer data), does Redwood guarantee data-at-rest and primary compute for hosted customers remain in an EU region (e.g. eu-west/ eu-central) or do any components (control plane, logging, analytics) transfer data outside the EU?
- If data does cross borders (control plane / backups / analytics), will Redwood provide a written bridge/interim letter explaining controls and compensating safeguards until the next SOC 2 is issued (we need something acceptable for our DPO and procurement)?
- Are there standard artifacts you can share (SOC 2 report, bridge letter, DPA snippet, list of subprocessors) and an expected timeline for delivery?

We appreciate concise, point-by-point replies — our procurement window is tight.

Thanks,
Caroline Larsen
Head of Third-Party Risk
EuroFin Trust
security@eurofintrust.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Larsen <caroline.larsen@eurofintrust.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:47:00 +0100
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II & hosting boundary questions

Caroline — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline below; looping in Marissa (Security) and Vivek (Compliance) to provide the formal artifacts and a bridge letter if needed.

- SOC 2 period: We completed a Type II audit for the period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30. Marissa will attach the full report and a short summary.
- Hosting boundary: For our Hosted product, primary customer data (object storage, model payloads, inference compute) is pinned to EU regions (we typically use eu-central1 or eu-west1 for EU accounts).
- Control plane & logs: Control plane metadata and some aggregated telemetry are processed in our control region (US). We segregate customer data and PII — customer data and persistent storage remain in the EU for EU-hosted accounts. We can provide an architecture diagram and the specific regions used for your tenant on request.
- Bridge/interim letter: Yes — we can provide a bridge/interim attestation describing the controls, dataflows, and compensating measures (encryption in transit & at rest, access controls, SCCs with cloud provider). Marissa — can you draft and attach the bridge letter and the SOC 2 PDF for Caroline?

Next steps: Marissa will share the SOC 2 PDF, a short bridge letter tailored for EU-hosted customers, and our DPA extract showing clauses about cross-border transfers and subprocessors. If EuroFin needs an account-level attestation (for dedicated/isolated deployments), we can scope that too.

Ben
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Larsen <caroline.larsen@eurofintrust.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: RE: SOC 2 Type II & hosting boundary questions

Hi Caroline — attaching the requested artifacts and a short narrative for procurement. See attachments: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026-06-30.pdf, Redwood-EU-Bridge-Letter-20260918.pdf, and DPA-extract-EU-hosting.docx. (Attachment stubs below.)

Summary / point-by-point:
- SOC 2: The attached Type II report covers the period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30 and is the latest available report. The next audit cycle is in progress; expected completion Q3 2027.
- Data localisation: For Hosted EU customers, persistent customer data and inference compute are provisioned in EU regions (we commonly use eu-central1).
- Control plane & telemetry: Our control plane services (multitenant management APIs, orchestration, and aggregated telemetry) run in a separate control region located in the US. We do not use control plane services to persist customer content outside the EU for Hosted EU accounts. Aggregated telemetry is pseudonymized and stored separately.
- Cross-border transfers & bridge letter: The attached bridge letter documents the controls and compensating measures for customers who require evidence during the gap between audits. It includes:
  * explicit confirmation that customer data for EU-hosted accounts remains in EU regions;
  * details on encryption (TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest) and key management;
  * subcontractor list and cloud provider SCCs;
  * recommended wording for procurement teams.

Attachments (stubs):
- SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026-06-30.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB)
- Redwood-EU-Bridge-Letter-20260918.pdf (PDF, 160KB)
- DPA-extract-EU-hosting.docx (DOCX, 45KB)

Notes / limitations:
- For Dedicated customers with on-prem or single-tenant network egress controls we can provide account-bound evidence and attestations; please confirm if EuroFin will be Hosted or Dedicated.
- The bridge letter is a stopgap artifact and not a replacement for the formal SOC 2 attestation; it is written to be accepted by procurement teams and DPOs as interim evidence.

Let us know if you need the architecture diagram with region-level endpoints (we can produce a tenant-specific diagram under NDA).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Security Director | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Caroline Larsen <caroline.larsen@eurofintrust.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 10:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II & hosting boundary questions

Marissa — thanks, the artifacts are exactly what we needed and the bridge letter language looks good to present to the DPO. A couple of follow-ups:

- EuroFin will be on the Hosted tier. Please confirm the canonical EU region you assign for new Hosted accounts (eu-central1 vs eu-west1) — we need that in our intake form.
- Could you also confirm whether backups are ever replicated to the US for DR purposes and, if so, whether those backups are encrypted and subject to the same access controls?

If you can add those two clarifications to the bridge letter or provide a short addendum, procurement will close this week. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Caroline
Head of Third-Party Risk
EuroFin Trust
